agent_summary: Ferritin is the one clear gap. Human evidence is strong (several sepsis cohorts, including a MIMIC-IV cohort of 718, link high ferritin to death). In dogs with babesiosis, ferritin was measured only in a 7-vs-7 seropositive case-control study (no difference) and in two case reports, and never against severity. A canine-specific ferritin immunoassay is in routine use. Hepcidin and serum iron/transferrin are not gaps, but the evidence is thin: hepcidin rests on one small Indian cohort (CH08, survivors vs non-survivors, probably confounded by species), and iron/transferrin has 4 units (CH08, CH12, CH07, CB112). One surprise: DS07 is the CB112 proteome, so its transferrin rows have already been tested by severity. Another: the local keyword list missed CB073 (CH07, lower iron in SIRS dogs) because that note says only 'iron'. No HU article bears on iron.

mechanisms.human_direction: mixed: raised by inflammation (higher in sepsis/septic shock; the hepcidin:ferritin ratio predicted septic-shock death, n=29), but suppressed in severe malarial anaemia compared with cerebral malaria (Kenyan children), so the direction depends on the phenotype

cb_confirmed.what: serum hepcidin (canine-specific sandwich ELISA, Sincere Biotech), 14 non-survivors vs 18 survivors vs 32 controls; higher in non-survivors (P<0.01), AUC 0.984 at 32.32 ng/mL; DOI https://doi.org/10.18805/ijar.b-4222 (not indexed in PubMed)

mechanisms.testable_detail: Not in DS07 (no master protein; the mature peptide is 25 aa and is unlikely to be seen in shotgun serum proteomics), HAMP not in DS06 counts, not in DS02. Canine LC-MS/MS (hepcidin-25 alpha and beta isoforms, reference interval 5.3-36.4 ng/mL) could be run on archived serum such as DS07's.
mechanisms.notes: The canine severity evidence is one unit only: a small single-centre cohort from a non-PubMed journal, with a cut-off derived in the same sample, a generic Chinese ELISA rather than the LC-MS/MS reference method, and mortality that depended strongly on species (mixed infections about 92%). The PubMed canine babesiosis search returned 0 records. A replication with LC-MS/MS in B. rossi or B. canis would add a lot of value, even though the rule-based gap is 'no'.

mechanisms.human_direction: higher in fatal sepsis/septic shock (MIMIC-IV n=718, OR 1.97 above 526 ng/mL; paediatric cohorts n=115 and n=123; septic shock n=79, https://doi.org/10.7759/cureus.115711); in malaria, ferritin is much higher in clinical than in asymptomatic infection (meta-analysis), but it is not independent of SOFA in some cohorts

mechanisms.testable_detail: Only DS06 whole-blood RNA-seq has FTL (ENSCAFG00000003861) and FTH1 (ENSCAFG00000015901, ENSCAFG00000030465). This is leukocyte/reticulocyte gene expression, not circulating ferritin protein, and it covers 5 experimental Beagles (time course, not a severity contrast). There is no ferritin master protein in DS07 and nothing in DS02. Serum ferritin itself would need stored samples (stored_samples_only for the protein).
mechanisms.notes: The 'validated' grade rests on a canine-specific ferritin immunoassay with published canine use in leishmaniosis, cardiac disease and fracture studies. This PubMed pass found no formal method-validation paper. CB132 raises haemophagocytosis/hyperferritinaemia as a lead for severe disease, which parallels human hyperinflammation.

mechanisms.human_direction: lower transferrin goes with death in sepsis (burn sepsis n=943, univariable). Higher, not lower, serum iron independently predicted 60-day death in septic ICU patients (n=133), so hypoferraemia itself is not a consistent severity marker in humans

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 master TF E2QZQ1 (33% coverage) and J9P430 (23%), TFRC F1PEN6 (8%); TFRC A0A0A0RBT6 and Q9GLD3 are master_candidate only (with a note). DS06 TFRC (ENSCAFG00000012941; gene expression, not protein). DS02 has no iron variables. DS07 is the CB112 dataset, so its transferrin severity contrast is already published.
mechanisms.notes: Serum iron and TIBC are generic colourimetric chemistry run on standard analysers (Roche Cobas in CH12), so the grade is used_in_dogs rather than a formal canine validation. Units: CH08 (CB202+CB286), CH12 (CB141), CH07 (CB073), CB112. The canine direction (lower iron and lower transferrin with severity) matches inflammatory hypoferraemia. Human sepsis data are inconsistent on serum iron. Transferrin saturation was never tested against severity in dogs.
